01 | The first call

YOU LOST THE MOMENT YOU ASKED FOR A FREE ESTIMATE.

Because before you know it, you can be choosing the best salesperson while the most important decisions about your home remain unanswered.

You want to know what your renovation will cost.

Fair question.

But has anyone measured the house? Worked through the layout? Understood how your family actually lives? Shown you what you’re agreeing to build?

If those things haven’t happened, what exactly is being priced?

That invitation for a “free estimate” can turn into a very polished sales presentation.

Confident answers. Beautiful project photos. An attractive starting number.

You start feeling good about the person across the table.

But feeling good about the salesperson and understanding your project are two very different things.

Who has worked out why your kitchen doesn’t function?

Whether moving that wall solves your problem?

Where your family needs more space, more privacy, better circulation?

What you should keep? What you should change? What you might regret?

Those questions require professional work. A persuasive presentation cannot answer them for you.

Yet you can find yourself discussing a construction contract while those decisions are still floating around in your imagination.

The person knows how to get your signature.

But how much do you actually know about the home you’re signing for?

DIRECTION: Oren to camera. Describe the risk of selecting on salesmanship before defining the project. Do not portray this as evidence that all free estimates or salespeople are unprofessional.

02 | Professional work before commitment

Your home deserves more homework than a sales pitch.

Before you commit to construction, put the design team to work.

Measure the existing house.

Work through the space.

Review the proposed layout.

See the design direction.

Ask questions. Make revisions. Understand what you’re choosing.

That is the work Ignite is built around.

Ignite is a paid design package that brings together measured information about your home, space planning, concept plans, visual direction and design revisions.

You have something concrete to examine, question and refine before committing to the main construction contract.

Construction pricing comes separately afterward. A construction quote or estimate is not included in Ignite.

Being convinced to sign should never replace understanding what you’re signing for.

Design Before Demo.

Start with Ignite.

DIRECTION: Show permission-cleared examples of the measured house, layout and concept work. This is paid design work; the initial meeting remains the introductory conversation.

03 | What the work gives you

If you are planning a full home remodel, a room addition or an ADU, here is what that design work includes.

04 | What Ignite actually includes

Ignite brings eleven connected pieces into one design package. Let me tell you exactly what they are.

First, the Design DNA Questionnaire. Written intake about your priorities, the way you live, and what the home has to get right.

Second, Live Sessions With the Design Team. Working conversations by video or in the design center, where you can ask questions and respond to the direction.

Third, a Matterport 3D Scan of Your Home. A measured digital twin of the existing house.

Fourth, As-Built Plans. Drawings of the home as it stands today, including walls, doors, windows and fixtures.

Those establish the starting point. Then we work through the design.

Fifth, Space Planning. The zones, circulation and use of each space. The layout has to work before the finishes can make sense.

Sixth, Concept Floor Plans. The proposed design drawn to scale, so you can discuss the arrangement on paper.

Seventh, Concept Images of Your Space. Two 3D conceptual designs of your key spaces. You can respond to a visual direction instead of trying to hold the whole house in your imagination.

Eighth, Mood and Concept Boards. Images, textures, colors, furniture and fixtures considered together.

Ninth, Color Palettes for Your Home. Coordinated schemes shaped around the mood you want to live in.

Then there is room to refine the direction.

Tenth, Design Revisions, up to three rounds. You can respond to what you see and work through the changes with the team.

And eleventh, Your Project Timeline. An approximate construction schedule informed by the design and the team's experience.

That is the package. Your priorities. The existing house. The layout. The visual direction. The opportunity to refine it. And a planning conversation about what comes next.

DIRECTION: Reveal the eleven names in this exact order. Use authentic deliverable examples with permission. No made-up values, bonuses or extra services.

05 | What that clarity is for

One homeowner, Jessica, described it this way:

“#IGNITE gave me an opportunity to visualize my home and choose the right path thanks to the accurate proposal and timeline.”

That is the kind of decision this process is intended to support. You can see a direction, discuss it, and decide whether it is the one you want.

But let me be clear about the limits.

Ignite does not include a construction quote or estimate. Construction is priced separately afterward.

The timeline is approximate. Existing conditions, permitting and changes to scope can still affect construction. Design work does not make every unknown disappear.

It gives us a chance to address the questions we can understand before work starts.

DIRECTION: Jessica.N, SoCal. Exact supplied testimonial; publication permission and attribution must be cleared. Keep the construction-quote exclusion on screen and legible.

06 | The fee, and the meeting

Ignite is one connected package with one flat fee, quoted in the meeting.

First, we discuss your project and whether the package fits. Then we explain the fee. You can ask your questions before deciding whether to move forward.

The meeting itself is free and obligates you to nothing.

You are scheduling a conversation about the project. There is no checkout and no application fee.

If Ignite is not the right fit, we will say so and point you toward the right first step.

That is our Straight-Answer Promise.

DIRECTION: Meeting, fee and promise language remain subject to operating approval. Earlier minimum-disclosure policy is unresolved; do not treat this draft as approval to conceal a required minimum.

07 | Who should take the next step

If you are planning a full home remodel, a room addition or an ADU, and you want to understand the design before committing to construction, this is a conversation worth having.

Ignite is not for one-room remodeling. And if all you want is a quick construction number without design work, it is not the right starting point.

Bring the questions that matter. Bring a few images if they help explain the direction. If you share the decision, have the other decision-makers join you. If you are deciding on your own, come yourself.

We will discuss what you want to change, what matters most, the budget you are considering and who is part of the decision.

Then we will give you a straight answer about the next step.

DIRECTION: Confirm the final meeting questions with Oren. No fabricated appointment slots or response-time claims.

You do not have to choose the whole home today.

But before you commit to building it, you should understand what you are choosing.

Let us talk about your home while the important decisions are still on paper.
